answer: A pigment-simulation market pays from a vault only for verified compute tickets, not for new accounts. Each ticket uses a wallet-bound challenge derived from the fresh beacon and a common deadline. The worker commits a memory-bound execution trace; random spot checks must pass before payout. Falcon may open a thousand aliases, but every paid ticket needs its own completed trace within that same window. Splitting one machine divides its capacity, while scaling the attack requires extra RAM, electricity and computation.
